in_arabic.name: داوس

in_arabic.long_meaning: داوس هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي و معناه: الدافع، الطارد، المطارد. وقد ورد في بعض الروايات أن النبي محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يدعو الله تعالى بالداوسية، أي بالدفاع والحماية من كل سوء. ويعتبر هذا الاسم من الأسماء ذات الأصول القوية في اللغة العربية.

in_urdu.name: داؤس

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun records the name of a Berber leader named Dawwas in his work 'The Muqaddimah', who ruled in the Maghrib (North Africa) around 1336-1356 AD. He was a powerful Zanata Berber chief who managed to extend his rule over a large part of the Maghrib, including the region of Tangier and its hinterland.

Al-Maqrizi, an Egyptian historian, mentions Dawwas in his book 'Ittifak al-Buldan' as a ruler of Ifriqiya (present-day Tunisia) in the late 5th/early 6th century AH (11th-12th century AD). He was a descendant of the Aghlabid dynasty and governed Ifriqiya during a period of instability and fragmentation, effectively establishing a new Berber state.
